title: Referrals and repeat work from existing clients for Dog walking
audience: Dog walkers who want repeat bookings and referrals from owners they have already served.
learningOutcomes: Plan a review or referral request that is made after the client confirms the result and that the client can decline easily.
Write a next-service offer with a date, a scope and a price approach, and schedule the check-in that follows it.
Write referral reward terms, including the condition for payment, before any referral is made.

instruction.heading: Ask once the owner is happy with the walks
instruction.body: The best time to ask for a review or referral is after the owner has confirmed the walks are going well, usually after a few weeks or at payment. Ask in one sentence, name the step you want (a review, or the name of one neighbour who might want walks), and make it easy to say no. Record what you asked and the reply. In one experiment, a late reminder brought in more reviews than an immediate one, but that was one study and not an Australian one (Baylor Keller Center, 1 June 2024). Google provides a review link or QR code that you can share. Never write reviews for owners, invent them, or ask only the owners you expect to be happy: a vendor source describes that as review gating, which Google treats as a violation (Podium, 2 May 2022). Google also bans discounts or goods in exchange for reviews (Google Business Profile Help, no date shown), and the ACCC says incentives must be disclosed and must not depend on what the review says (ACCC, 15 July 2026).

instruction.heading: Offer the next walk before the owner leaves
instruction.body: Repeat work is a reliable source of income for a walker, but the research found no Australian figure for repeat-booking rates, so do not assume how often owners return. At the end of each walk period, propose the next step with a date: a weekly walk on the same days, a set number of walks a week, or a holiday walk plan. Put the scope, the interval and the price in writing, and confirm that the owner agrees before you change the schedule. If the offer goes by email or text, check the electronic message rules first. ACMA's guidance indicates that inferred consent is narrow and does not cover a message sent just after a purchase (ACMA, no date shown).

instruction.heading: Check in at a set interval
instruction.body: Schedule a check-in after a period that suits the service. For walks, about ninety days is a starting point to test, not a benchmark. The check asks whether the arrangement still suits, whether anything has changed, and whether there is other work to quote. Keep it short and record what the owner said. A message that only asks about the walks may not be commercial, but a message that promotes any service can be commercial, even when it is framed as a reminder (Clayton Utz, 9 November 2023). Check the rule before you send.

instruction.heading: Re-contact owners before their busy periods
instruction.body: Plan a short message a few weeks before the periods you can see in your own bookings, such as school holidays. No Australian source for holiday or seasonal demand for dog walking was found, so set the dates from your own calendar. Offer the slots you can deliver, on written terms, with a clear way to opt out. ACMA says an unsubscribe must be honoured within five working days (ACMA, no date shown), so record each opt-out as soon as you receive it and stop sending to that owner.

instruction.heading: Set referral rewards in writing before anyone refers
instruction.body: A referral reward works best when the owner knows the terms before they refer someone. Decide what you will offer, such as a credit on the next walk, and write down the payment condition, which is normally that the referred owner has completed a paid walk. In seven studies, stating the referrer's reward in the invitation increased referrals (Xu, Yu and Tu, Journal of Marketing Research, 2023), so say what the reward is in the invitation. Get the referred person's consent before any referral message is sent, because the referrer's word alone may not be enough (Clayton Utz, 2017; an older source). The tax and contract effect of a reward is UNCONFIRMED: no business.gov.au or ACCC guidance on referral rewards was found. Check any cash reward with an adviser before you start.

procedure: After each booking is confirmed, make one review or referral request and record what was asked and the reply.
Write the next-walk offer with the days, scope, interval and price approach, and confirm it with the owner.
Schedule a check-in about ninety days after the last walk, and send it under the electronic message rules.
Plan a re-contact message before each busy period in your own calendar, and exclude anyone who has opted out.
Write the referral reward and its payment condition before the first referral is made.
When a referred owner completes a paid walk, apply the reward and record the outcome.

workedExamples.situation: A walker has looked after one owner's two dogs for four months, three walks a week. The owner says she will recommend the walker to her sister, who lives in the same street. The walker would like to offer a credit on the next walk if the sister books.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What should the walker write down before the sister books, and what should he avoid?
workedExamples.reasoning: He writes the credit, the payment condition (the sister completes a paid walk) and the date the credit is applied, and gives the owner a copy. He asks the owner to pass on the sister's details, and contacts the sister only if she agrees. He does not promise a reward he has not written down. If he is unsure of the tax or contract effect of a credit, he checks with an adviser. A referral does not extend his permit, licence or insurance, so he takes on the sister's dogs only within those and within the council rule on the number of dogs.

equipmentAndPpe: Client record with the booking date and the review or referral request made
Next-walk offer template with days, scope, interval and price approach
Calendar of re-contact dates built from your own bookings
No PPE is needed for client follow-up; any walk follows your own safety checklist

commonErrors.error: Asking for a review before the owner has confirmed the walks are going well
commonErrors.prevention: Ask after the owner confirms the service, or at payment.

commonErrors.error: Offering a referral reward that was never written down, so its terms are disputed later
commonErrors.prevention: Write the reward and its payment condition before any referral, and give the referrer a copy.

commonErrors.error: Publishing an owner's name, photo or review, or a dog's details, without consent
commonErrors.prevention: Get consent for each thing you plan to publish, and keep the record.

commonErrors.error: Contacting an owner who asked not to hear from you, or using a message to pressure them
commonErrors.prevention: Keep an opt-out list, honour it at once, and keep messages factual and optional.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Publishing an owner's name, photo, review or a dog's details needs the owner's consent for that use. Do not write reviews on an owner's behalf or invent them. If the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) applies to your business, owner details are personal information. Check the OAIC small business guidance to see whether it applies to you.

Review platforms and referral programmes can have their own rules on incentives. Google bans discounts or goods in exchange for reviews, and the ACCC says incentives must be disclosed. Check each platform's rules before you offer a reward.

Check-in and re-contact messages sent by email or text can be commercial electronic messages under the Spam Act 2003 (Cth). ACMA has been enforcing this area. The Spam Act text was not read for this research, so check it before you send.
A referral does not extend the permit, licence or insurance of the walker. Accept only the walks your permit, any licence and your insurance cover, in the council or state where the walk takes place.

qualityStandard: Every review or referral request is made after the owner confirms the service or pays, and includes an easy way to decline.
Every next-walk offer is written, dated and confirmed by the owner before the schedule changes.
Every referral reward has written terms and a payment condition, and is paid only when that condition is met.
documentationEvidence: Review or referral request log, with the date sent and the reply
Next-walk offers with the date, scope, interval and owner confirmation
Referral reward terms with the referral record and payment outcome
summary: Ask for reviews and referrals after the owner confirms the service, and make it easy to say no.
Offer the next walk in writing, with a date, before the owner leaves.
Set referral rewards and their payment conditions in writing before anyone refers.

knowledgeChecks.question: When is the best time to ask a client for a review or referral?
options: Before the first walk, so the owner feels committed
After the owner has confirmed the walks are going well
Only when the owner has sent you a complaint

knowledgeChecks.question: An owner wants to post a review with her name and a photo of her dog. What do you need?
options: Her consent for the name and photo you plan to publish
Nothing, because the review is positive
Your own judgement that the photo looks professional

knowledgeChecks.question: What should a referral reward look like?
options: Paid to anyone who mentions your name
Decided after the referred owner books, based on how keen the referrer seems
Decided and written in advance, with the payment condition stated

knowledgeChecks.question: When does the lesson say to propose the next walk?
options: At the end of each walk period, with a date

ACCC, 'Online reviews for product and services', https://www.accc.gov.au/business/advertising-and-promotions/online-reviews-for-product-and-services, published and updated 15 July 2026.

Podium, 'Review gating', https://www.podium.com/article/review-gating, 2 May 2022. Vendor source; the Google position was not checked against Google's own policy.

Xu, Yu and Tu, Journal of Marketing Research 60(2), 2023, https://research.polyu.edu.hk/en/publications/i-will-get-a-reward-too-when-disclosing-the-referrer-reward-incre/. Stating the referrer reward in the invitation; no figures used.
Clayton Utz, 'Referrer beware', https://www.claytonutz.com/insights/2017/may/referrer-beware-proceed-with-caution-when-contemplating-refer-a-friend-promotions, 11 May 2017. Older than 2022.

Clayton Utz, 'The ACMA cranks up enforcement', https://www.claytonutz.com/insights/2023/november/the-acma-cranks-up-enforcement-do-your-factual-customer-emails-pass-the-spam-act-test, 9 November 2023.
ACMA, 'Avoid sending spam', https://www.acma.gov.au/avoid-sending-spam, no date shown; read 2026-11-03 or 2026-11-04 per the research file.
Gap: no Australian data on repeat-booking rates or referral rates for dog walkers was found. The Baylor figure comes from one experiment and is not an Australian rate.
Gap: no business.gov.au or ACCC guidance on referral rewards was found; the tax and contract effect of rewards is UNCONFIRMED.

OAIC small business guidance summary read in the targeted-search research file, 13 May 2026: https://www.oaic.gov.au/privacy/australian-privacy-principles-guidelines/. Small business coverage is UNCONFIRMED there.

officialReferences.title: ACMA, Avoid sending spam
officialReferences.covers: Recorded from the team4 research files (read 2026-11-03 or 2026-11-04), not reopened: marketing messages need consent, and consent should be recorded; each message identifies the sender, and its unsubscribe works for 30 days and is honoured within five working days. Does not mention one-to-one messages.
